script.base: Week 7 Miami at Cleveland, outdoor, 1:00 ET, closing line CLE -2.5 and total 34.5, so the book expects a close grind with Cleveland 18.5 and Miami 16.0. Cleveland should lean on Quinshon Judkins, who has 56 carries and 228 yards over weeks 4-6, into a Miami run defense that has allowed 5.78 yards per carry and 32 runs of 10-plus in six games. Joe Flacco's dropbacks stay inefficient: Jerry Jeudy has 27 targets, only 106 yards and 332 air yards in that same window, and Miami blitzes 41 percent, where Flacco's EPA per dropback is -0.42. Miami, only a 2.5-point dog, is not in a forced pass script. De'Von Achane still touches the ball (46 carries, 243 yards, plus 15 targets) but Cleveland's run defense allows 3.35 yards per carry, and the Miami pass game that does show up is Jaylen Waddle (23 targets, 253 yards, 305 air), not Tyreek Hill (6 targets, 67 yards, 40 air in the same three weeks).
script.flip1: Cleveland leads by two scores and clocks it with Judkins. That helps the rush over and hurts Miami's run game, so Achane's 58.5 rush line dies the way a trailing back's carries die. Flacco's attempts fall, which makes Jeudy's 45.5 receiving under easier, not harder. Chase-script risk is on the Miami side only: Waddle and Darren Waller targets can rise, and a late Hill spike is the way a Miami receiving under would lose. Spread is 2.5, so a true benching blowout is the tail, not the base.
script.flip2: Miami hits explosives — Cleveland has allowed 19 gains of 20-plus yards for 183 yards — and leads. Judkins' carry total stalls toward the 36-yard game already on his last four, and Flacco is forced into extra dropbacks against that 41 percent blitz. Checkdowns to Harold Fannin Jr. (20 targets, 118 yards with David Njoku still active) and Jerome Ford (10 targets, 37 yards, negative air) rise. Jeudy's under loses only if those extra dropbacks finally convert the 332 air yards, which is the live risk because S Elijah Campbell is out.

injury_fallout: Official pre-game nflverse report, not the 90-minute inactive list. CLE TE David Njoku is Out (knee) after 18 targets, 106 yards and 106 air yards in weeks 4-6. Same-position gain is Harold Fannin Jr., already at 20 targets and 118 yards while Njoku played; secondary absorbers are Jeudy (27 targets), Isaiah Bond (18 targets, 96 yards, 215 air), Ford and Judkins (7 targets, 51 yards). That Njoku redistribution is why a Jeudy under is a lean, not a strong: some of those 18 targets can land on the WR1. CLE T Jack Conklin is Questionable (concussion); if he sits, Judkins' efficiency path off 4.07 YPC weakens. CLE DE Joe Tryon-Shoyinka, DT Mike Hall Jr. and DT Mason Graham are Questionable, so Cleveland's 3.35 YPC run-defense log cannot be treated as full strength until inactives — that is why Achane rush under 58.5 is not a carded leg. CLE WR Gage Larvadain Questionable is depth. MIA S Elijah Campbell is Out (quadricep): missing safety helps deep shots, which is the direct counter to fading Jeudy and the modest boost for Bond. MIA LB Tyrel Dodson is Questionable (concussion); if he sits, TE and RB catches (Fannin, Ford, Judkins) get easier. MIA CB Storm Duck is Questionable (ankle). Hill is not on the report. Waller, Malik Washington, Julian Hill and Tanner Conner have no out tag.

matchup.shell: No MOFO/MOFC or man/zone charting was saved, so shell is inferred from six-game location splits only. Cleveland pass defense: left 6.32 YPA on 65 attempts, middle 10.11 YPA on only 19 attempts, right 6.93 YPA on 85 attempts. Perimeter is sound; the middle is the bleed on a tiny sample. Miami pass defense: left 7.47 YPA on 72, middle 6.75 on 32, right 9.03 on 70. Miami's pass soft spot is the right side, not the middle where a tight end would live.
matchup.pressure: Cleveland blitzes only 23 percent. Tua's EPA per dropback is +0.12 with no blitz and -0.08 when blitzed, so Miami's pass game is not pressure-suppressed — that is the environment Waddle's 305 air yards have been living in, and it is not a reason to fade him today. Miami blitzes 41 percent. Flacco is -0.42 EPA per dropback versus the blitz and still -0.19 with no blitz. Pressure is the Cleveland passing kill switch: it cuts Jeudy's 12.3 air yards per target and Bond's 11.9, and it pushes the ball to Fannin, Ford (already negative air yards) and Judkins.
matchup.bleeds: Miami bleeds on the ground: 5.78 yards per carry and 32 runs of 10-plus in six games, against only 11 such runs allowed by Cleveland. That is the Judkins overlap. Cleveland's pass bleed is explosives (19 of 20-plus, 183 yards) plus a 19-attempt middle sample at 10.11 YPA, not the perimeter. Miami's pass bleed is the right side at 9.03 YPA. Neither defense is a dome shootout unit; the total is 34.5 for a reason.
matchup.overlap: Judkins is Cleveland's primary rushing option and he runs exactly where Miami gives it up. Jeudy is Cleveland's primary target by volume (27 targets) but he does not attack a soft zone — he attacks air yards into the blitz, which is a negative overlap and the under. Waddle is Miami's primary target and the best candidate for Cleveland's middle and explosives, but alignment is uncharted, so he is not carded. Fannin does not attack Miami's right-side or run bleed; his case is Njoku's absence plus checkdowns, which is a sleeper note, not the overlap.

form: Avoiding season averages and using weeks 4-6 plus the listed last-four. Judkins last-four rush yards 94, 82, 110, 36; the three-week sum is 228, so weeks 4-6 are 82, 110 and 36 (76.0 per game) on 18.7 carries at 4.07 YPC. Volume is the stable fact; the 36 is the floor. Achane last-four rush 62, 99, 16, 128 and 46 carries for 243 yards (5.28 YPC, 81 per game) — form is hot and the Cleveland run defense plus questionable DTs are why that form is not an over. Waddle last-four 39, 48, 110, 95; 48+110+95 = 253, matching his three-week total, so the recent games are 48, 110 and 95 against a 58.5 median. Hill's four played games are 40, 109, 49 and 67 (265 yards) but only 67 of those yards fall in weeks 4-6, so he was mostly absent, not a proven two-target-a-game decoy — do not treat 58.5 under as a role collapse. Jeudy last-four 17, 48, 15, 43; 48+15+43 = 106, matching the three-week total, so recent games are 48, 15 and 43 (mean 35.3) on 27 targets and 332 air yards. Fannin last-four 25, 24, 13, 81; 24+13+81 = 118, so the recent mean 39.3 is the 81-yard spike, not a stable over. Ford 8 carries for 34 yards. Ollie Gordon 11 carries for 9 yards. No new play-caller is in the pack.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and the card lost. Judkins finished under 82.5 because Conklin was inactive, Miami sold out to a back who had just run 56 times in three weeks, and the 36-yard game was the template — 15 carries, low-4s YPC, Ford taking the goal-line looks in a 17-16 game that never became a clock-kill, so 4.07 times 18 never got the matchup bump and landed near 74. Jeudy went over 45.5 because Campbell was out, Duck was inactive, one of the 332 air yards finally hit for 40, and Njoku's targets gave him two extra catches on a day Flacco was not as bad as the -0.42 blitz split. The stand-ins were their own medians, so there was no closing number to blame. That counter is why Jeudy is a lean and why the Judkins strong read stays flagged for the human instead of sized.
slip_story: One Cleveland control story in a 34.5 outdoor game: the home favorite runs Judkins into the Miami run bleed, and Flacco's deep shots to Jeudy do not cash against a 41 percent blitz. Both legs win together in the base and in flip 1. Do not add Fannin or Bond overs, a Waddle over, or a game total over — those need flip 2 or a Hill-absence target share this card is not betting.
